- **`seeds/cosmogram-research-prompt.md`** (501 lines): Complete one-shot research briefing for generating deck cosmograms. Contains:

  - 12 operators as organizational principles for documents

## Implementation Details

The research prompt uses dense specification format (tables, nested categories, polysemic definitions) to carry complete SCL-61 context in working memory during research sessions. It is designed to be pasted directly into AI chat with web search access.

The publication standard establishes that PPL± is a living publication with 1,680 editorial voices, each derived from the four-emoji zip code structure. This makes the system self-documenting: the zip code itself encodes the editorial character that should shape content at that address.

Both documents are written in the established PPL± voice: learned, direct, economical, civic in posture, and designed to survive scrutiny across multiple reading depths (surface, moderate, complete).

## Summary

This PR improves graceful failure handling in `incr` and reduces panic-oriented call patterns.

### Problem
- Batch closures that raise should not leave pending runtime state.
- Callers needed to pattern-match `Result` everywhere to avoid panic-oriented APIs.

### Solution
- Added transactional rollback for raised errors in batching:
  - `Runtime::batch(self, f: () -> Unit raise?) -> Unit raise?`
  - `@incr.batch(db, f)` updated to match
- Added explicit `Result` batch helper:
  - `Runtime::batch_result(self, f: () -> Unit raise?) -> Result[Unit, Error]`
  - `@incr.batch_result(db, f)`
- Added non-panicking convenience reads:
  - `Memo::get_or`, `Memo::get_or_else`
  - `MemoMap::get_or`, `MemoMap::get_or_else`
- Added rollback plumbing for batched signals (`rollback_pending`) and invariant-safe cleanup paths.

### Tests
- Expanded/added tests for:
  - raised-error rollback behavior
  - nested rollback behavior
  - post-rollback reusability
  - helper API behavior (`batch_result`)
  - non-panicking read convenience APIs
- Full suite passes: `193/193`.

## Summary
Fixes a post-deploy verification false-negative in release tag pipelines.

Pipeline `#162` failed in `release-deploy-pages` even though all four `wrangler pages deploy` commands completed successfully. The verifier loop reported `stage=missing` for all projects until timeout.

## Root Cause
`tools/verify-pages-deploy.sh` assumed a strict metadata/environment shape when reading `wrangler pages deployment list --json`:
- strict commit key/format matching only
- strict environment assumption (`stable -> production`)

In real responses, metadata can vary by key naming and hash length, and environment visibility can differ from assumption.

## Changes
- Hardened commit metadata matching in `tools/verify-pages-deploy.sh`:
  - Supports `commit_hash`, `commitHash`, `commit_sha`, `sha`, `commit`
  - Supports short/full hash matching
  - Adds commit-message fallback (`PAGES_COMMIT_MESSAGE`) when needed
- Added environment fallback in `auto` mode:
  - `stable`: `production -> preview -> all`
  - non-stable: `preview -> production -> all`
- Added `PAGES_VERIFY_ENVIRONMENT` override:
  - `auto|production|preview|all`
- Expanded summary output with matched env/branch/commit for easier diagnosis
- Updated docs + ledger:
  - `apps/docs-site/docs/operations/release-automation-mac-mini.md`
  - `docs/changes.md`

## Validation
- `bash -n tools/verify-pages-deploy.sh`
- `bun run docs:check`

## Changes

Closes https://github.com/withastro/astro/issues/15656 
 
I noticed the following warning in my Astro project:

```
[Shiki] 10 instances have been created. Shiki is supposed to be used as a singleton, consider refactoring your code to cache your highlighter instance; Or call `highlighter.dispose()` to release unused instances.
[Shiki] 20 instances have been created. Shiki is supposed to be used as a singleton, consider refactoring your code to cache your highlighter instance; Or call `highlighter.dispose()` to release unused instances.
[Shiki] 30 instances have been created. Shiki is supposed to be used as a singleton, consider refactoring your code to cache your highlighter instance; Or call `highlighter.dispose()` to release unused instances.
```

This is due to the fact that Astro creates a new Shiki highlighter instance for each language, and there are many different code block languages in my project. 

This PR improves this by using the same highlighter across languages. This approach works because Astro already loads languages dynamically when they haven't been loaded yet ([code link](https://github.com/withastro/astro/blob/a7b1410da36747686a5b64c854d635a0ab370b0d/packages/markdown/remark/src/shiki.ts#L121-L124)).


## Testing

Added a new test to ensure that 

1. The same highlighter instance is used for different languages. body:
`ProjectAdmin` had no inline visibility into the `RemoteRepository` connected to a project via the `remote_repository` FK. Admins had no way to inspect the remote repository details without navigating away from the project page.

## Changes

- **`readthedocs/projects/admin.py`**: Added `RemoteRepositoryInline` (read-only `StackedInline`) to `ProjectAdmin`
  - Displays `full_name`, `clone_url`, `html_url`, `private`, `vcs`, `vcs_provider`, `default_branch` as read-only fields
  - `show_change_link = True` for direct navigation to the remote repository admin page
  - No add/change/delete permissions — view-only via `ReadOnlyInlineMixin`
  - Collapsed by default (`classes = ["collapse"]`)

- **`readthedocs/oauth/admin.py`**: No changes (reverted to original state)

Since `Project.remote_repository` is a FK from `Project` → `RemoteRepository` (not the reverse), Django's standard inline mechanism cannot be used directly in `ProjectAdmin`. The implementation overrides `check()` to skip the FK system check and overrides `get_formset()` to use a `modelformset_factory`-based formset whose queryset is built from the project's `remote_repository_id`:

```python
class RemoteRepositoryInline(ReadOnlyInlineMixin, admin.StackedInline):
    model = RemoteRepository
    classes = ["collapse"]
    fields = ("full_name", "clone_url", "html_url", "private", "vcs", "vcs_provider", "default_branch")
    readonly_fields = fields

    @classmethod
    def check(cls, parent_model):
        # No FK from RemoteRepository to Project; handled manually in get_formset()
        return []

    def get_formset(self, request, obj=None, **kwargs):
        qs = RemoteRepository.objects.filter(pk=obj.remote_repository_id) if obj and obj.remote_repository_id else RemoteRepository.objects.none()
        ...
```

## **User description** 💡 **What:** Optimized the global `mouseover` listener in `CustomCursor.tsx` by implementing two key strategies: 1. **Throttling:** Wrapped the event processing logic in `requestAnimationFrame` to limit execution frequency to the screen refresh rate (max 60fps), preventing excessive CPU usage during rapid mouse movements. 2. **DOM Query Optimization:** Combined multiple `element.closest()` calls into a single query (`closest('button, a, [data-hover="true"]')`) for interactive elements, reducing DOM traversal overhead while maintaining precedence for custom cursor text. 3. **Refactoring:** Moved mutable state (`rafId`, `lastTarget`) to `useRef` to ensure robustness against React re-renders and correct lifecycle management. 🎯 **Why:** The previous implementation performed up to 4 separate DOM traversals on every `mouseover` event. body:
## Summary
- Fixes the React error #310 crash on the `/gallery` page and homepage gallery lightbox
- Increases the green "Now accepting applications" announcement banner size

## Root Cause (React #310)

`useBaseUrl()` is a React hook, but it was called **inside a conditional render block** (`{currentImage && (...)}`) in the lightbox sections of both:
- `src/pages/gallery.tsx` (line 257)
- `src/components/Gallery/index.tsx` (line 120)

**What happened:**
- Lightbox closed → `currentImage` is `null` → `useBaseUrl()` **not called** (0 extra hooks)
- Lightbox opened → `currentImage` is non-null → `useBaseUrl()` **called** (1 extra hook)
- Hook count changed between renders → React error #310: "Rendered more hooks than during the previous render"

**Why it worked locally before:** The previous fix commit was on the branch but was dropped during the squash-merge of PR #31, so main never received the fix.

## Fix

Moved `useBaseUrl()` to the **top level** of each component, called unconditionally:
```tsx
const lightboxSrc = useBaseUrl(currentImage?.src ?? '/');
```
The hook now runs on every render regardless of lightbox state, satisfying React's Rules of Hooks.

## Announcement Banner

Added CSS to increase the green announcement bar padding and font size:
- Mobile: `padding: 1rem`, `font-size: 1.125rem` (18px)
- Desktop (1024px+): `padding: 1.5rem`, `font-size: 1.25rem` (20px)

## Files Changed
| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/pages/gallery.tsx` | Move `useBaseUrl` out of conditional block |
| `src/components/Gallery/index.tsx` | Same fix for homepage gallery |
| `src/css/custom.css` | Announcement bar sizing styles |

## How to Reproduce (before fix)
1. Go to live site → click "Gallery" in navbar
2. Page crashes: "Minified React error #310"

## Validation
- [x] Gallery loads in DEV without errors
- [x] `npm run build` succeeds
- [x] Gallery loads in PROD serve (port 3333) without errors
- [x] Lightbox open/close/prev/next works on both `/gallery` and homepage
- [x] Announcement banner visibly larger

## Overview

Adds a full-screen setup wizard that runs on first launch (and can be re-opened from Settings). It guides users through checking and configuring every runtime dependency before the main app appears.

## Steps

| # | Step | What it does |
|---|------|-------------|
| 1 | Welcome | Shows GPU & memory summary |
| 2 | Models | Confirms resolved models directory path, existence, and write access |
| 3 | Engine | Installs llama.cpp pre-built binaries with live SSE progress bar |
| 4 | Downloads | Provisions the Python hf_xet fast-download virtualenv |
| 5 | Complete | Summary of each step; writes `setupCompleted=true` to settings |

Every step has a **Skip** button so users are never blocked.  
The Python step has a prominent **Retry** button with the full error message displayed on failure.

### Motivation
- Provide a dynamic retention engine that computes cohort retention from `cohort_membership` and `events_normalized` on-demand rather than precomputing or storing metrics.
- Expose a simple API to retrieve retention buckets `0..max_day` so callers can analyze day-by-day active user percentages per cohort.

### Description
- Added a new `GET /retention` endpoint (`get_retention`) with a `max_day` query parameter (default `7`) that returns the retention matrix JSON for all cohorts.
- Implemented SQL-based activity delta computation using `DATE_DIFF('day', join_time::DATE, event_time::DATE)` and aggregated distinct active users per `(cohort_id, day_number)` up to `max_day`.
- Aggregated cohort sizes with a `LEFT JOIN` on `cohort_membership` so cohorts with zero members are included, and computed percentages in Python returning `0.0` when appropriate.
- Added `tests/test_retention.py` with scenarios for basic retention, multiple cohorts, `max_day` behavior, and empty-cohort response, and updated `README.md` to document the endpoint.

Makes `CUDA_COMPILER` a variable that can be set when initializing `SpaceSFFT_CupyFlow` object or directly calling resampling kernels.   This is motivated by wanting to use the `nvrtc` backend on systems where the `gcc` version is not compatible with the CUDA library version.  Previously the backend was hardcoded to `nvcc`. # Pull Request — SAACGAS

## Summary
- Summary: Add token to api, add authenticate to server, update authzContext to rely on authenticate. This forces all calls to backend to be authenticated by cognito.

## Related issue(s)
<!-- Link related issue numbers, e.g. `Closes #123` or `Relates to #456` -->
- Closes #39 

## Type of change
- [ ] Bug fix

- [ ] Other: ______

---

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- **Does this change affect** authentication, authorization, encryption, or key management?
  - [X] Yes — explain below
  - [ ] No
- **Does this change process or store user data, model outputs, or secrets?**
  - [X] Yes — explain below
  - [ ] No

If Yes to either: describe what changed and why, list new secrets/keys (if any) and where/how they are stored, and provide mitigation steps and test evidence.

Security notes / mitigations:
Threat model changes:
Authentication is now enforced on all protected routes via authenticate.js middleware. Every request must carry a valid Cognito ID token. Unauthenticated requests are rejected with a 401 before reaching any route handler. /api/health is intentionally left public for monitoring purposes.
Cryptography used / changed:
JWT verification is handled by aws-jwt-verify which validates tokens against Cognito's public keys (RS256). No custom cryptography is used. The previous code used jwt.verify with a JWT_SECRET which was incompatible with Cognito-issued tokens and has been removed.
Secrets handling and rotation plan:
Two new environment variables are required: AWS_COGNITO_USER_POOL_ID and AWS_COGNITO_CLIENT_ID. These are not secrets — they are public identifiers. No private keys or secrets are stored server-side. Token signing and rotation is handled entirely by AWS Cognito.
Logging/observability changes that affect privacy:
The previous code logged "Token is invalid" on failed verification. The new authenticate.js does not log token contents or user identifiers on failure, reducing risk of leaking sensitive data to logs.

The AI assistant always started with `apiKey: null`, causing every feature (Documentation Packet, chat, appeal letters, coverage predictor) to return a system error object whose `response` string was then rendered as if it were real AI output.

## Changes

### Developer-side key pre-configuration (`js/env.js` + `js/xai-huggingface-integration.js` + `index.html`)
- New `js/env.js` (committed empty placeholder) — developer sets their X.AI key here once; all users share it transparently:
  ```js
  window.MEDHELPER_XAI_KEY = 'xai-your-key-here';
  ```
- `DualAIMedicalTeam` constructor now reads `window.MEDHELPER_XAI_KEY` at construction time so the key is active before any user interaction.
- `index.html` loads `js/env.js` before AI scripts, then runs `syncDevKey()` to mirror the key into `appConfig` so `anyConfigured` returns `true` and all AI-gated paths execute.

### Prevent error responses bleeding into UI (`covered-conditions.js`, `script.js`, `document-analyzer.js`, `index.html`)
All `getTeamResponse` call-sites previously used `result.response || ''`, which treated the error object's message string as valid content. Every call-site now guards against the `error` flag:

```js
// Before — error message rendered as AI output
const result = await window.aiTeam.getTeamResponse(prompt);
responseText = result.response || '';

// After — falls through to rule-based fallback
responseText = (!result.error && result.response) ? result.response : '';
```

`covered-conditions.js` returns `null` on error responses so the Documentation Packet correctly falls back to its "AI unavailable" message instead of displaying the system prompt.

2. Claim History must display a list of past claims associated with the policy, showing: Claim Number, Date of Loss, Claim Status.
3. Claims must be sorted by Date of Loss (most recent first) and filterable by Claim Status (Open, Closed, Paid, Denied).
4. Add/Edit policy information at claim level when policy is unverified; changes must be tracked separately and not overwrite original policy data.
5. Visual indicator must show when claim-level policy information is being used.
6. Audit log must track all changes to claim-level policy data, including user and timestamp.
7. Claims must support referral to subrogation and management of scheduled payments (applicability, type, total amount, balance, current due, recipient identification).
8. Claims must support injury incident details, coding information, and carrier involvement.

Payments & Disbursements
************************
1. Payments must be linked to claims and policies, supporting multiple payment methods: ACH, wire, credit/debit card, Stripe Connect, global payouts.
2. Support onboarding of vendors and claimants with secure payment method verification (including KYC/Identity).
3. Enable automated creation of payable line items from external estimates (e.g., Xactimate/XactAnalysis).
4. Allow configuration of payment routing rules based on payee, payment type, and business rules.
5. Provide full payment lifecycle management: creation, voids, reversals, reissues, reserve handling.
6. Enable allocation of payments across multiple reserve lines and management of joint payees.
7. Support creation of Electronic Funds Transfers (EFT) and wire transfers with required banking details.
8. Allow creation of payments with positive, negative, or zero dollar amounts.
9. Support designation of payments as eroding or non-eroding against reserve lines.
10. Enable management of multiple payment details per transaction (add/remove payees, payment portions, deductions).
11. Allow withholding of income tax and designation of payments as tax reportable; capture tax ID numbers for payees.
12. Support document attachment to payment transactions.
13. Remittance & Medical Payments: Support EDI/EOB-style remittances to medical providers, including CPT/ICD mappings and adjustments; integrate with bill review vendors and support EDI 835/837 formats.
14. Negotiation & Settlement Management: Provide negotiation management, coverage opinion requests, and settlement plan tracking.
15. Compliance: Ensure PCI-DSS compliance, mask sensitive payment information, encrypt all payment data in transit and at rest, maintain audit trail for all payment actions and changes.

Integration Requirements
************************

1. Integrate policy, claims, and payment modules for seamless workflow.
2. Integrate with external systems: Stripe Connect, Global Payouts, Bank ACH/Wire, Xactimate/XactAnalysis, Accounting, Bill Review, EDI 835/837, Litigation Data, Tax ID, General Ledger, Agency Markets Payment Service, Document Management.
3. Capture and reuse Other Carrier Information across claim functions, including parties and payments.

Non-Functional Requirements
***************************

1. All interfaces must be responsive and optimized for workflow efficiency.
2. Policy search results must be returned within 3 seconds; policy details and claim history within 5 seconds; payment processing within 5 seconds.
3. System must support concurrent user sessions without performance degradation.
4. All integrations must be robust and support error handling and retry logic.
5. Display must be accessible and compliant with WCAG guidelines.

Error Handling & Messaging
**************************

1. If no matching policies or claims are found, display: "No matching policies/claims found."
2. If the system is unavailable, display: "System is currently unavailable."
3. If policy/claim/payment details cannot be retrieved, display: "Unable to retrieve details. Please try again later."
4. If claim-level policy data cannot be saved, display: "Unable to save claim-level policy data. Please try again later."
5. If no prior claims exist, display: "No prior claims exist for this policy."

Security
********

1. Mask and encrypt sensitive data (SSN/TIN, payment info).
2. Enforce role-based access control.
3. Maintain comprehensive audit logs for all actions.

Audit & Compliance
******************
1. All changes to policy, claim, and payment data must be tracked with user and timestamp.
2. System must comply with PCI-DSS and other relevant standards.

Complete implementation of a university attendance tracking system where students mark presence by scanning QR codes, validated against their physical location using the Haversine formula.

### Database Schema
- `users.role` enum: admin, enseignant, etudiant
- `cours`: courses linked to teachers
- `seances`: sessions with unique 64-char QR tokens, time slots
- `presences`: attendance records with GPS coords, distance, status (present/retard/absent)

### Backend
- **GeolocationService**: Haversine distance calculation, enforces 300m radius from university (33.225410, -8.486408)
- **Controllers**: CRUD for courses/sessions, attendance validation with dual frontend+backend geolocation check
- **CheckRole middleware**: Route protection by user role
- **Form Requests**: French validation messages

### Frontend (React + shadcn/ui)
- **Student**: Dashboard with stats, pointage page with real-time GPS indicator, attendance history
- **Teacher**: Course/session CRUD, QR code display with copy/regenerate/download
- **Admin**: Global statistics, CSV export

### Key validation flow
```php
// Backend always validates location (never trust frontend)
$locationCheck = $this->geolocationService->verifierLocalisation($lat, $lon);
if (!$locationCheck['estDansLeRayon']) {
    return response()->json(['success' => false, 'message' => '...'], 422);
}
```

author: ids1024
body:
This avoids the need to directly depend on `wayland-backend` to enable these. This seems generally good. There shouldn't be any harm in having these features, with the caveat that we can't use the absence of the feature in the higher-level crate to make assumptions about what backend is in use.

Adding backend related features to `wayland-client`/`wayland-server` also part of my plan for adding feature flags for `libwayland` versions, for things like https://github.com/Smithay/wayland-rs/pull/735 and https://github.com/Smithay/wayland-rs/pull/855:

- Add features like `libwayland_server_1_22` to `wayland-backend` and `wayland-sys`
- Then have a feature like `libwayland_1_22 = ["wayland-backend/libwayland_server_1_22"]` in `wayland-server`
- The functionality in `wayland-server` will be restricted to only apply when the `libwayland_1_22`
- If `system`/`server_system` isn't used, the `libwayland_1_22` feature will still be required, but `libwayland-server` will not actually be needed

The last point is a bit awkward, but it's the best way I can think of the keep the features correctly additive, and also allows a wayland compositor to use new server features with the `rs` backend without requiring a particular version of `libwayland-client` for the `winit` backend of the compositor.

## Summary
Improve PDF readability in the “Information Sharing, Travel & Photo / Media” area by reducing excessive vertical whitespace in the long policy paragraphs while preserving the approved PDF layout and table borders.

## Problem
The PDF rendering for “Information Sharing, Travel & Photo / Media” contained excessive vertical whitespace in policy paragraph blocks. After tightening, the first consent sentence needed a small separation from the following paragraph for readability.

## Root Cause
TCPDF does not reliably respect CSS margin/padding within the policy paragraph markup, resulting in unintended vertical spacing. Tight inline-span rendering is more predictable in TCPDF.
